candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.46(a). The previous permit will be expired on October 31, 2021. The permittee submitted their application to EPA on April 13, 2021. The existing permit is administratively continued until this permit is issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether FY2025 measurements are evaluated against the administratively continued prior permit or the reissued permit depends on when the new permit was issued relative to the monitoring period; this changes which numeric limits and permit conditions are operative.

candidates.exact_span: NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When multiple limit sources could apply to a parameter, the selected enforceable numeric limit depends on which source is deemed more stringent; a different reading of comparability or stringency changes the limit used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS and BOD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This assigns TSS and BOD to technology-based limit derivation rather than water-quality-based or other bases; misclassification would change which numeric limits are treated as applicable for those parameters.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for E. coli bacteria, pH and TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This assigns E. coli, pH, and TRC to water-quality-based limits rather than technology-based limits; a different interpretation of parameter classification would change the applicable numeric limits and whether a numeric compliance comparison is available.

candidates.exact_span: numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: The numerical versus narrative distinction affects whether an enforceable numeric limit exists for comparison; for parameters with only narrative limits, missing numeric results may be classified as non-comparable rather than as missing required monitoring evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require TBELs to be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of guidelines, or on a combination of the two.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The basis for deriving technology-based limits—ELG, BPJ, or a combination—determines which numeric values are selected when guidelines are partially applicable or absent.

candidates.exact_span: In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether promulgated guidelines are absent for a given discharge determines whether BPJ-derived limits apply instead of ELG-based limits, changing the enforceable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: EPA establishes limitations based on the following technology-based controls: BPT, BCT, and BAT.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable technology level (BPT, BCT, or BAT) governs which treatment standard and corresponding numeric limit are used for technology-based parameters.

candidates.exact_span: BPT - The first level of technology-based standards generally based on the average of the best existing performance facilities within an industrial category or subcategory.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If BPT is the operative standard, the limit value depends on interpretation of 'best existing performance' and the relevant industrial category or subcategory; different readings change the derived numeric limit.
